transcript:
Meeting: Heliograph FinOps & Route Analytics Walkthrough
Date/Time: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Alicia (Heliograph Head of ML), Marcus (Platform Eng), Sana (FinOps)

--- Auto Summary (may be auto-generated) ---
Maya: Quick summary: this call is a console walkthrough focused on per-route cost and usage analytics, finishing with next steps to set up a pilot.

--- Topics ---
- Route-level cost attribution
- Dashboard drilldowns and exports
- Alerts for spend anomalies
- Private vs hosted routing considerations
- Security checklist (SSO/KMS/audit)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alicia, Marcus, Sana, good to see you. We're going to walk through the Redwood Console usage and per-route cost stuff — and show a few examples of how you can map routes to product features for FinOps. Jonas and I will tag-team.
[00:18] Alicia: Great, thanks. We only have an hour, so wanna focus on the billing mapping, and also how to alert on weird spikes — last quarter we had a weird token surge.
[00:29] Jonas: Yep, we'll show the spike detector and how the console ties to invoicing. Quick note — demo tenant will have synthetic traffic but mirrors your route names if you give us the mapping.
[00:41] Marcus: Sounds good. I emailed a sample routes.csv last night, hope you got that.
[00:46] Maya: Yep got it, that helped. Alright Jonas, take it away on the dashboard.
[00:52] Jonas: Cool. I'm sharing my screen — give me two secs to pull up the per-route lens.
[01:03] [01:03] Jonas: Ok, here is the main usage page — top left is overall token volume and cost, then per-route breakdown. You can change the time window, group by model, region, or route.
[01:18] Jonas: Notice the color-coded stack — each route is a band. You can hover to see model, tokens, and cost. The console computes estimated cost by mapping tokens to model profiles and GPU pricing.
[01:33] Sana: How accurate is that cost estimate vs our invoices? We have custom discounts and committed spend.
[01:40] Maya: Good question. The console uses Redwood's internal cost model for hosted. For Dedicated we show both actual GPU-hours and normalized per-token numbers. We can ingest your billing CSV to align numbers and apply commit discounts.
[01:55] Marcus: So we would upload our billing export and then reconcile? Is that manual?
[02:01] Jonas: It's a one-time mapping step — you upload CSV, point fields, the Console suggests mappings, you confirm. After that reconciliation is automatic each day.
[02:12] Alicia: Can we do route-level tagging based on our internal feature flags? We have nested routes, featureA.v2 etc.
[02:19] Jonas: Yes, tag mapping supports regex and prefixes. You can also map multiple routes to a single product line. The dashboard will show both the raw route list and the grouped product view.
[02:31] [02:31] Jonas: Let me click into a single route — this view shows tokens by input vs output, model used for each call, latency distribution, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:44] Jonas: You can add filters for status codes or error type which helps correlate spikes.
[02:49] Alicia: That latency chart is handy — we've had some tail latency incidents. Can Redwood route to a lower-cost quantized variant automatically if latency is acceptable?
[02:57] Maya: We have smart routing policies — you can configure cost vs latency preferences. For example, route X can prefer a cheaper quantized model, but if latency or quality thresholds fail, it falls back to the native FP32 variant.
[03:11] Marcus: And does the console show the fallback events?
[03:15] Jonas: Yes, each request log shows which backend handled it — so you can count fallbacks per route and per time window.
[03:22] [03:22] Jonas: Now looking at costs tab — here's cost by model family and route. You can pivot to show cost per feature, or per-team owner, if you attach tags.
[03:33] Sana: Can we export to our internal FinOps tool? We use Snowflake and a custom ETL.
[03:38] Jonas: Sure. You can export a daily CSV or push to an S3 bucket. We also have a scheduled export API that streams records into your data lake.
[03:47] Sana: Does it include token-level traces or aggregated metrics?
[03:51] Jonas: Both. By default it's aggregated (per-route/day/model), but you can opt-in for request-level logs (we caution about PII and retention).
[04:02] Alicia: About retention — we need 1 year of aggregated metrics and 90 days of request logs, is that doable?
[04:08] Maya: Hosted default is 90d for request logs and 1y for aggregates on paid plans; for Private deployments you can configure retention or integrate with your own storage.
[04:19] Marcus: On Private, how does KMS integration work? We have an HSM and strict key rotation.
[04:25] Jonas: We support KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys for the private control plane. Audit logs are shipped to your SIEM. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys and an option for BYOK for enterprise customers.
[04:39] [04:39] Alicia: Let's talk anomaly detection — show me the spike example.
[04:43] Jonas: Yep. In the Alerts panel you can create an anomaly detector based on token-rate or cost. We support simple thresholds and learned baselines. Here is an example: last month we detected a token surge on route /chat/assist — console flagged deviation of 3 stds and sent a slack alert.
[05:00] Jonas: The alert links to a runbook with suggested mitigations: limit rate, throttle token budget per user, route-specific fallback.
[05:09] Sana: Good. Can alerts be emitted to PagerDuty and Slack?
[05:13] Jonas: Both, plus webhook endpoints and email. You can map alert severity to escalation.
[05:19] [05:19] Alicia: About mapping routes to products — we want the cost to appear on our team chargeback dashboard. How do we ensure tokens are attributed correctly when clients do multi-route calls?
[05:30] Maya: Two options: you can use explicit route-level metadata in requests, or use post-hoc attribution using request traces and the mapping rules. We recommend adding a header or metadata field in calls for perfect attribution.
[05:44] Marcus: For the pilot we won't be able to change all clients. Can Redwood do a heuristic mapping?
[05:50] Jonas: Yes, we can run a windowed reconciliation that uses path heuristics and user id to attribute calls; accuracy can be ~95% depending on your patterns.
[05:59] [05:59] Jonas: Now I'll demo the per-route cost drilldown and the 'what-if' cost simulator.
[06:05] [06:05] Jonas: The simulator lets you flip model variants (e.g., small -> quantized) and shows estimated monthly savings given your request distribution. It uses real usage to simulate.
[06:18] Alicia: That's super helpful. Can it include committed discounts and reserved capacity?
[06:23] Jonas: You can add your committed spend terms into the simulator so the outputs include commit-adjusted pricing.
[06:29] Sana: For budgeting we need forecasted costs for next quarter with and without the pilot. Can we export a scenario report?
[06:35] Jonas: Yes, scenario exports are PDF/CSV that span model mix, route grouping, and expected SLO impacts.
[06:44] [06:44] Marcus: A question on scale — our busiest route gets 20k rps at peak. How does Redwood handle batching and KV cache at that scale?
[06:53] Jonas: We support continuous batching and KV cache sharding. For high QPS routes we recommend Dedicated pools with autoscale. The Console surfaces per-backend utilization so you can see saturation and split traffic across multiple pools.
[07:06] Maya: If you run privately on-prem we can also provide a planning guide for GPU sizing — Jonas can share that after the call.
[07:14] [07:14] Jonas: Now switching to the Optimize tab — this provides recommendations: suggested batching window, quantization profile, and a candidate model list sorted by cost/quality tradeoff for your corpus.
[07:27] Jonas: Each recommendation shows expected token-savings and estimated impact on latency and quality (we use your eval prompts to approximate).
[07:36] Alicia: Are the quality estimates from Redwood verified with a holdout prompt set? We can't risk hallucination regressions.
[07:44] Maya: We tie recommendations to your evals if you upload them. We also support A/B rollouts with automatic rollback if quality drops beyond a threshold.
[07:56] [07:56] Marcus: For the A/B tests — is traffic split in the runtime and can we keep sticky sessions?
[08:03] Jonas: Yes, runtime does sticky routing at the request-id level and supports warm-up of KV caches. Rollouts can be canary percentages or per-user cohorts.
[08:12] Sana: If we see unexpected quality drift during rollout, can we pause automatically and notify the team?
[08:18] Jonas: Absolutely — that's built into the rollout policy.
[08:23] [08:23] Alicia: Let me ask about audit logs — for compliance we need an immutable log of every model version deployed and rollout changes.
[08:31] Maya: Audit trails include deploy events, policy changes, and user actions in the Console. For enterprise we can forward those to your SIEM; logs are tamper-evident in Private deployments.
[08:43] [08:43] Marcus: Back to cost: when we convert to Dedicated pools, how do we see amortized GPU cost vs per-token?
[08:52] Jonas: The Console shows both amortized GPU-hour cost and per-token normalization. It also shows utilization heatmaps — you can see idle vs active time and get recommendations for packing models.
[09:03] Jonas: There is also a reserved capacity planner that simulates commit levels and suggests pool sizes to minimize unit cost.
[09:13] Alicia: For our pilot, we're mostly interested in hosted but may shift to Dedicated if costs look favorable. What are the commit windows?
[09:21] Maya: Typically monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts; we have short-term burst options too. We can include both in the pilot proposal.
[09:29] [09:29] Marcus: Any docs on the token accounting? We need to map our internal token metric to Redwood's.
[09:35] Jonas: Yes — we have a Token Accounting guide that explains how we count tokens for different model families and how streaming responses are accounted. I'll attach that.
[09:44] Sana: Can we demo a real spike detection on our sample data? Marcus uploaded a CSV.
[09:50] Jonas: Let's ingest it into the demo tenant. (pause) Ok ingested — here's the generated anomaly chart — you can see the sudden jump on May 12. The console suggests the top contributing routes and the model mix at the spike.
[10:08] Alicia: Looks like /generate-batch was the culprit. Good to know.
[10:12] Jonas: The console can also retroactively attribute cost to a date range and generate a post-mortem export.
[10:19] [10:19] Jonas: Quick aside: privacy — request-level logs are redacted by default for PII; you can configure redaction rules.
[10:27] Alicia: Ok, this looks promising. A few clarifying product questions — will Redwood mark which routes are eligible for quantized variants?
[10:36] Jonas: Yes, the model catalog marks compatibility and also has performance profiles per sequence length. The Console will flag where quantizing might degrade quality.
[10:46] Maya: We should also surface potential regression risk in the scenario report.
[10:50] Jonas: We do that — a confidence score and recommended eval prompts to run during canary.
[10:58] [10:58] Marcus: Anything on latency SLO monitoring in the Console?
[11:03] Jonas: Latency SLOs can be defined per-route, with percentiles tracked and alerting.
[11:09] Sana: For billing exports — if we use S3 push will it be encrypted with our KMS?
[11:15] Maya: Yes, you can configure server-side encryption with your KMS key. For Private we can wire it into your HSM.
[11:24] Alicia: One final question on ownership — our finance team wants a neat chargeback CSV per-team. Can the Console produce invoice-ready CSVs?
[11:32] Jonas: Yes, invoice-ready exports are a feature on the enterprise plan; they include mapped routes, grouped lines, and your applied discounts. You can export monthly or for a custom date range.
[11:44] [11:44] Maya: Okay, wrapping up demos. Quick recap and next steps. Sana — you'll send the billing export. Marcus — confirm demo route mapping file if any changes. From Redwood, Maya will send pilot pricing, Jonas will provision the demo tenant and attach the Token Accounting guide.
[11:59] Alicia: Sounds good. Who will we talk to for security pack?
[12:03] Maya: I'll cc our security lead, Priya, and include SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration checklist.
[12:10] Sana: Great. Timing for pilot kickoff?
[12:14] Maya: We proposed 2026-07-27 for a 30-min kickoff once the demo tenant is ready.
[12:19] Alicia: Works for us.
[12:22] [12:22] Jonas: Any other blockers?
[12:25] Marcus: No, just internal finance sign-off but that's normal.
[12:29] Maya: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[12:34] Alicia: Thanks, talk soon.
